nodes.description: Public string state variable 'question' holding the riddle text shown to players.
Address state variable 'questionSender' acting as the game owner/admin.
bytes32 state variable 'responseHash' storing keccak256 of the correct answer.
external payable Try(string _response): requires msg.sender == tx.origin and pays out the whole balance when the answer hash matches and msg.value > 0.5 ether.
public payable set_game(string _question, string _response): one-time initialization of responseHash, question and questionSender when responseHash == 0x0.
public payable StopGame(): only questionSender may call; drains the entire contract balance to msg.sender.
public payable NewQuestion(string _question, bytes32 _responseHash): questionSender can replace question and responseHash.
public newQuestioner(address newAddress): questionSender can transfer ownership to a new address.
payable fallback function that silently accepts ether sent to the contract.
msg.sender: caller-controlled address used for authorization checks and as the payout recipient.
tx.origin: transaction origin used in Try as an authorization/anti-contract gate.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside Try: sends the entire contract balance to the caller (external value call).
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside StopGame: sends the entire contract balance to the owner (external value call).
keccak256(_response) == responseHash check inside Try, the answer verification gate.
keccak256(_response) computation in set_game that seeds responseHash.
Parameter _response (string) of Try; the raw answer supplied by the caller.
Parameter _question (string) of set_game; initial riddle text.
Parameter _response (string) of set_game; hashed to create responseHash.
Parameter _question (string) of NewQuestion; new riddle text.
Parameter _responseHash (bytes32) of NewQuestion; new answer hash.
Parameter newAddress (address) of newQuestioner; the successor owner address.

edges.reason: Try reads responseHash to compare it with keccak256(_response).
Try consumes msg.sender in the require(msg.sender == tx.origin) gate.
Try authorizes the caller against tx.origin, making authorization depend on the transaction origin.
Caller-supplied _response is hashed by the keccak256 check in Try.
The stored responseHash is the left-hand side of the comparison in Try.
The full-balance transfer in Try only executes when the answer hash matches and msg.value > 0.5 ether.
Try performs an external value transfer to the untrusted caller, which can re-enter the contract through its fallback.
set_game stores msg.sender as questionSender during initialization.
The _response string is consumed by keccak256 inside set_game.
The hash produced in set_game is written into responseHash.
The _question parameter is written into the question state variable.
set_game grants ownership by writing questionSender from msg.sender.
StopGame authorizes the caller by reading questionSender.
StopGame compares msg.sender with questionSender to restrict draining to the owner.
StopGame reaches the balance transfer only after the owner check passes.
StopGame transfers the whole balance to msg.sender via an external call that can trigger a callback.
NewQuestion reads questionSender to authorize the caller.
NewQuestion compares msg.sender against questionSender before updating state.
The _question parameter overwrites the question state variable in NewQuestion.
The _responseHash parameter overwrites responseHash in NewQuestion.
newQuestioner reads questionSender to authorize the ownership transfer.
newQuestioner compares msg.sender against questionSender.
The newAddress parameter becomes the new questionSender, an ownership handover.
newQuestioner writes the questionSender state variable.
The payable fallback accepts ether from the untrusted caller.
The transfer to msg.sender can invoke the recipient's fallback/callback while the balance is being drained.
The StopGame transfer to msg.sender can invoke a recipient callback during the balance drain.
